# VibePicks
> Editorial rankings of the best AI tools for vibe coders and builders shipping apps, grouped by use case. Ranks are editorial picks, not paid placements.

Full version with every tool, pricing label, plain-English reason and release: https://vibepicks.ai/llms-full.txt
Each category page also has a plain Markdown copy for AI agents, e.g. https://vibepicks.ai/coding-agents/index.md
New releases as Markdown: https://vibepicks.ai/releases/index.md
Agents can also ask for Markdown directly: request any category page (or the homepage) with the header Accept: text/markdown, e.g. curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://vibepicks.ai/coding-agents/
Last updated: 2026-10-28

## Coding Agents & AI IDEs (https://vibepicks.ai/coding-agents/)
1. [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code): Terminal-based agent for multi-file changes in real repos (Paid)
2. [Cursor](https://cursor.com): AI-first code editor for building and refactoring whole apps (Freemium)
3. [OpenAI Codex](https://chatgpt.com/codex): Delegating coding tasks to a cloud or CLI agent (Freemium)
4. [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot): Inline completions and agent mode inside VS Code and GitHub (Freemium)
5. [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai): Open-source coding agent that works with any AI model (Free)
6. [Google Antigravity](https://antigravity.google): Google's agent-first coding app and CLI (Freemium)
7. [Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)](https://devin.ai/desktop): Agentic IDE for running and managing local and cloud coding agents (Freemium)
8. [Grok Build](https://x.ai/build): Terminal-based coding agent from xAI (Freemium)

## App Builders (https://vibepicks.ai/app-builders/)
1. [Lovable](https://lovable.dev): Prompt-to-full-stack web app with Supabase integration (Freemium)
2. [Bolt.new](https://bolt.new): In-browser prompt-to-app builds you can run and deploy (Freemium)
3. [v0](https://v0.app): Generating React/Next.js UI and apps from prompts (Freemium)
4. [Replit](https://replit.com): Cloud IDE with an agent that builds and hosts apps (Freemium)

## Deploy & Hosting (https://vibepicks.ai/hosting/)
1. [Vercel](https://vercel.com): Deploying Next.js and frontend apps from Git (Freemium)
2. [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com): Static sites and Jamstack apps with simple deploys (Freemium)
3. [Cloudflare Workers & Pages](https://www.cloudflare.com/products/workers/): Free global hosting for static sites, plus Workers for server code (Freemium)
4. [Railway](https://railway.com): Deploying backends, workers, and databases with little config (Freemium)
5. [Render](https://render.com): Hosting web services, cron jobs, and Postgres (Freemium)

## Auth (https://vibepicks.ai/auth/)
1. [Clerk](https://clerk.com): Drop-in sign-in UI and user management for React/Next.js (Freemium)
2. [Supabase Auth](https://supabase.com/auth): Auth bundled with your Supabase Postgres database (Freemium)
3. [Better Auth](https://better-auth.com): Free, open-source auth that keeps users in your own database (Free)
4. [Auth0](https://auth0.com): Enterprise-grade auth, SSO, and identity (Freemium)
5. [Firebase Authentication](https://firebase.google.com/products/auth): Simple auth for mobile and web apps on Google's stack (Freemium)

## Payments & Email (https://vibepicks.ai/payments-email/)
1. [Stripe](https://stripe.com): Accept card payments, subscriptions and checkout links (Paid)
2. [Resend](https://resend.com): Send emails from your app: receipts, sign-ups, password resets (Freemium)
3. [Paddle](https://www.paddle.com): Sell software and subscriptions with sales tax handled for you (Paid)
4. [Polar](https://polar.sh): Sell digital products, licenses and subscriptions, tax handled (Paid)
5. [Postmark](https://postmarkapp.com): Reliable transactional email for important messages (Freemium)

## Databases & Backend (https://vibepicks.ai/databases/)
1. [Supabase](https://supabase.com): Postgres, auth, storage, and realtime in one backend (Freemium)
2. [Firebase](https://firebase.google.com): Realtime NoSQL backend for quick mobile/web apps (Freemium)
3. [Neon](https://neon.com): Serverless Postgres with branching (Freemium)
4. [Convex](https://www.convex.dev): Reactive TypeScript backend with built-in database (Freemium)
5. [PlanetScale](https://planetscale.com): Scalable managed MySQL/Postgres (Paid)

## Design-to-Code (https://vibepicks.ai/design-to-code/)
1. [Figma Make](https://www.figma.com/make/): Turning prompts and Figma designs into working prototypes (Freemium)
2. [Builder.io](https://www.builder.io): Converting Figma designs into framework code (Freemium)
3. [Locofy](https://www.locofy.ai): Figma/Penpot to React, Next.js, and mobile code (Paid)
4. [Anima](https://www.animaapp.com): Exporting Figma designs to React/HTML code (Freemium)

## Testing & QA (https://vibepicks.ai/testing/)
1. [Playwright](https://playwright.dev): Reliable end-to-end browser tests (open source) (Free)
2. [Cypress](https://www.cypress.io): Developer-friendly E2E and component testing (Freemium)
3. [Sentry](https://sentry.io): Catching errors and crashes in production (Freemium)

## AI Code Review (https://vibepicks.ai/code-review/)
1. [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai): AI code review on pull requests (Freemium)
2. [Greptile](https://www.greptile.com): AI code review that understands your whole codebase (Freemium)
3. [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot): Automatic AI review on GitHub pull requests (Paid)

## LLM APIs (https://vibepicks.ai/llm-apis/)
1. [OpenAI API](https://platform.openai.com): General-purpose GPT models for chat, tools, and vision (Paid)
2. [Anthropic API](https://claude.com/platform/api): Claude models, strong at coding and long context (Paid)
3. [Google Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev): Gemini models with large context and multimodal input (Freemium)
4. [xAI API](https://x.ai/api): Grok models plus image, video and voice on one API key (Paid)
5. [DeepSeek API](https://api-docs.deepseek.com): Low-cost models with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs (Paid)
6. [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai): One API key to route across many model providers (Freemium)

## AI Images & Art (https://vibepicks.ai/ai-images/)
1. [ChatGPT Images](https://chatgpt.com/images): Quick images and edits by chatting (Freemium)
2. [Nano Banana (Gemini)](https://gemini.google/overview/image-generation/): Make and edit images by chatting in the Gemini app (Freemium)
3. [Midjourney](https://www.midjourney.com): High-quality illustrations and artistic images (Paid)
4. [FLUX (Black Forest Labs)](https://bfl.ai): Photo-real images and an image API with open models (Paid)
5. [Ideogram](https://ideogram.ai): Logos, stickers, posters and images with readable text (Freemium)
6. [Grok Imagine](https://grok.com/imagine): Quick images from a sentence, right inside Grok (Freemium)
7. [Recraft](https://www.recraft.ai): Logos, icons, vector art and brand sets (Freemium)
8. [Leonardo](https://leonardo.ai): Emotes, game assets, characters and stylized art (Freemium)

## AI Audio & Voice (https://vibepicks.ai/ai-audio/)
1. [Suno](https://suno.com): Songs, jingles and background music from a text description (Freemium)
2. [ElevenLabs](https://elevenlabs.io): Realistic AI voiceovers, narration, sound effects and music (Freemium)
3. [Descript](https://www.descript.com): Edit podcasts and videos by editing the transcript (Freemium)

## AI for Hardware & Electronics (https://vibepicks.ai/ai-hardware/)
1. [Arduino Cloud](https://cloud.arduino.cc): Write, upload and control Arduino/ESP32 projects with a built-in AI assistant (Freemium)
2. [Wokwi](https://wokwi.com): Simulate Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi Pico projects in your browser (Freemium)
3. [Tinkercad](https://www.tinkercad.com): Beginner circuits and 3D-printable designs (Free)
4. [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com): Explain wiring, write firmware and troubleshoot step by step (Freemium)
5. [Flux](https://www.flux.ai): AI-assisted circuit and PCB design (Paid)
6. [OpenPLC](https://autonomylogic.com): Free, open-source PLC you can program with ladder logic (Free)

## AI Video & Clips (https://vibepicks.ai/ai-video/)
1. [CapCut](https://www.capcut.com): Edit shorts and reels with auto captions (Freemium)
2. [Opus Clip](https://www.opus.pro): Turn a long video or stream into short clips (Freemium)
3. [Gemini Omni (formerly Veo)](https://gemini.google/overview/video-generation/): Realistic AI video clips with sound, made and edited by chatting (Paid)
4. [Kling AI](https://kling.ai): Make AI video clips from text or a picture (Freemium)
5. [Descript](https://www.descript.com): Edit video by editing the transcript (Freemium)
6. [Runway](https://runway.com): Generate short AI video clips from text or images (Freemium)
7. [Grok Imagine](https://grok.com/imagine): Short AI video clips with sound from text or a picture (Paid)

## Automations & Agents (https://vibepicks.ai/automations/)
1. [Zapier](https://zapier.com): Connect apps with simple if-this-then-that steps (Freemium)
2. [Make](https://www.make.com): Visual drag-and-drop automations (Freemium)
3. [n8n](https://n8n.io): Powerful automations and AI agents you can host yourself (Freemium)
4. [Grok Bot](https://x.ai/bot): AI teammates that work in your apps and run routines on a schedule (Paid)

## Websites & Stores (https://vibepicks.ai/websites/)
1. [Wix](https://www.wix.com): AI-built business websites with drag-and-drop editing (Freemium)
2. [Shopify](https://www.shopify.com): Online store to sell products (Paid)
3. [Framer](https://www.framer.com): Good-looking sites and landing pages with AI layouts (Freemium)
4. [Squarespace](https://www.squarespace.com): Polished templates for a simple business site or shop (Paid)

## Writing & Marketing (https://vibepicks.ai/writing/)
1. [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com): Draft posts, emails and product descriptions (Freemium)
2. [Claude](https://claude.ai): Natural-sounding writing and rewrites (Freemium)
3. [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com): Drafts and rewrites, built into Gmail and Google Docs (Freemium)
4. [Grok](https://grok.com): Timely social posts and replies (Freemium)
5. [Grammarly](https://www.grammarly.com): Fix spelling, grammar and tone as you type (Freemium)

## CAD & Machining (https://vibepicks.ai/cad-machining/)
1. [Fusion](https://www.autodesk.com/products/fusion-360/personal): CAD and CAM in one, from design to toolpaths (Freemium)
2. [Onshape](https://www.onshape.com): Browser-based CAD that runs on any computer (Freemium)
3. [Zoo Zookeeper](https://zoo.dev/zookeeper): Describe a part in words and get an editable 3D CAD model (Freemium)
4. [Tinkercad](https://www.tinkercad.com): Very simple 3D designs for printing (Free)
5. [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com): Explain and draft G-code, feeds and speeds (Freemium)

## Recent releases
- 2026-10-28: GitHub Copilot — Copilot Fusion is generally available: pick Fusion in the model picker and Copilot routes and combines models for each task instead of you choosing one, with Standard, High and Max effort levels. GitHub says Fusion Max scored within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at about half the cost. On all Copilot plans in VS Code, the Copilot app, Copilot CLI and JetBrains (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-route-and-orchestrate-models-with-github-copilot-fusion/)
- 2026-10-28: GitHub Copilot — Copilot cloud sessions now follow you everywhere: start a cloud agent task on github.com, GitHub Mobile, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, VS Code, Slack or Teams and pick it up on any of the others while it keeps running in a cloud sandbox. Sandbox time can come out of your included Actions minutes. Generally available on paid Copilot plans, rolling out from Oct 28; Copilot Projects for multi-repo goals are in public preview (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-work-from-anywhere-with-a-new-connected-copilot-cloud-experience/)
- 2026-10-28: GitHub Agentic Workflows — GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available: write an automation (issue triage, CI failure analysis, docs updates, test writing) as a plain-English Markdown file and it compiles to a normal GitHub Actions workflow run by Copilot or your own coding agent, read-only by default and sandboxed. On GitHub Free, Team and Enterprise; the default Copilot CLI engine needs a Copilot license (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-github-agentic-workflows-generally-available/)
- 2026-10-28: Supabase — OrioleDB is in public beta on every Supabase plan: an open-source Postgres storage engine built for tables with lots of updates and deletes, cutting the table bloat and VACUUM tuning the default engine needs. Choose it when you create a project; billed like standard Postgres, backups and read replicas work, but not ready for production yet (https://supabase.com/blog/orioledb-public-beta)
- 2026-10-28: Vercel — The Vercel Plugin now works in OpenCode 2: install it with opencode plugin add github:vercel/vercel-plugin to get Vercel skills (AI SDK, Functions, Workflow), /vercel:deploy and /vercel:env commands, and the Vercel MCP server so the agent can see your projects, deployments and logs (https://vercel.com/changelog/vercel-plugin-now-available-in-opencode)
- 2026-10-27: Supabase — Supabase Compute is in private alpha: run AI agents, background jobs and APIs (Node, Deno or any Dockerfile) inside your Supabase project, next to your Postgres data, for minutes or hours instead of the 400-second Edge Function limit. Deploy with supabase compute push (CLI v2.120.0+); free during the alpha, us-west-2 projects only, waitlist required and not for production yet (https://supabase.com/blog/supabase-compute-private-alpha)
- 2026-10-27: Replit — Replit Cloud Agents let anyone on a team describe a change in plain English, watch it in a live preview of the running app, and have the agent open a tested pull request on GitHub (or merge request on GitLab) that follows the team's guidelines and keeps fixing it as review comments come in. Engineers still approve what ships. Available now on Pro and Enterprise (https://replit.com/blog/anyone-can-bring-ideas-to-company-codebase)
- 2026-10-27: Cursor — Cursor design mode adds Annotate: give the agent visual prompts by editing elements, drawing right on the page, and reviewing your design at different screen sizes (https://x.com/cursor_ai/status/2115159585548021814)
- 2026-10-27: Gemini API — Google released the Gemini API CLI (gemini-api) in beta, a stateless, zero-dependency command-line client built for AI coding agents, scripts and CI pipelines. It uses the Interactions API to generate text and media, analyze files and run Gemini managed agents (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog)
- 2026-10-27: Ramp Inspect — Ramp opened early access to Inspect, the cloud coding agent its own teams use: hand it a task from Slack, GitHub, Linear, the web or your phone (even a screenshot with "@inspect fix this") and it returns a visually checked, reviewed pull request. Sessions are multiplayer so teammates can jump in and steer. Ramp says it now writes 74% of the company's merged PRs (https://ramp.com/blog/introducing-inspect)
- 2026-10-27: Vercel — Vercel Observability now shows AI traffic: requests by each verified AI bot, the pages AI crawlers hit most, pages AI assistants fetch in answer to a user's question, Markdown requests, and pages that return errors to bots. Find it under Observability > AI Traffic; querying it from the CLI with vercel metrics needs Observability Plus (https://vercel.com/changelog/ai-traffic-insights-now-available-in-vercel-observability)
- 2026-10-27: OpenCode — OpenCode v2.2.0 adds experimental desktop plugins you can create, install and share, a refreshed desktop app, experimental image-generation APIs for plugins, keyed session instructions that survive compaction without busting the prompt cache, and prompt-cache lifetimes you can set per provider and model. Heads-up: the OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published, so remove it from your workflows (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.2.0)
- 2026-10-26: GPT-6.1 Terra (OpenAI) — OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, lower-cost model for computer use, visual reasoning and writing. On the API as gpt-6.1-terra at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output (half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol), with a 1M-token context; also in ChatGPT and Codex for paid plans, and generally available in GitHub Copilot (https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/)
- 2026-10-26: Cursor — Cursor's Agent SDK is generally available: define an agent as a folder (instructions.md for the prompt, tools/ in TypeScript, skills, MCP connections), test it with built-in evals, and deploy it to Cursor with agent-sdk deploy or run it on your own servers. Agents can wake on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket events, Slack messages, webhooks or a schedule (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-sdk)
- 2026-10-26: GitHub Copilot — Assisted permissions are generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and VS Code: an AI model checks each command, file path or URL Copilot asks to use, lets clearly safe ones run, and still asks you about the rest. It's a middle ground between approving everything by hand and Allow All (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-26-github-copilot-assisted-permissions-generally-available/)
- 2026-10-26: Claude Code — v2.1.311 fixes long sessions stopping with "Usage credits required for 1M context" past 200K tokens (it now compacts and keeps going), fixes multi-thousand-line edits stalling for up to 5 seconds, lets subagents use MCP servers that connect late, and typing ultrathink mid-turn now raises effort for the rest of that turn (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.311)
- 2026-10-26: Entire — Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke's Entire launched a Git hosting platform built for coding agents: Trails replace pull requests with agent-scored checks on every push, Continuous Memory saves agent sessions into the repo so agents can search past work, and Buildkite and Depot handle CI. Open to every developer today, with private repos only for now (https://entire.com/news/entire-launches-an-independent-git-forge-for-agent-human-collaboration)
- 2026-10-26: Gemini API — New paid-tier projects now store Generate Content API requests by default (store=true), matching the Interactions API; opt out per request with store=false or in Logs and Datasets settings (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog)
- 2026-10-26: Vercel — Faster pnpm installs: dependency verification is reused across deployments, cutting average install time 14% on Pro, automatic on all plans (https://vercel.com/changelog/faster-pnpm-installs)
- 2026-10-26: Replit — Replit now works fully in Japanese, from the interface to prompts and agent output (https://x.com/Replit/status/2114587332137664535)
- 2026-10-25: Cloudflare WAF — Cloudflare added two emergency Managed Ruleset rules for the Node.js Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (memory leak or code execution when decoding attacker-controlled Brotli data): one matches Brotli-encoded request bodies, one matches the Next.js image optimizer path /_next/image. Both default to Log, not Block. If you self-host Next.js or any Node app, upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 (https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-25-emergency-waf-release/)
- 2026-10-23: Vercel Connect — Vercel Connect can now create a separate restricted Stripe API key for each agent or task (Managed API Key method), limited to the permissions you pick, so an agent never holds your full-access secret key. Vercel stores the key, and you can rotate it without redeploying (https://vercel.com/changelog/vercel-connect-adds-managed-stripe-api-keys)
- 2026-10-23: GitHub Copilot — The new GitHub app for Microsoft Teams combines notifications with Copilot: @mention GitHub on a bug report in a channel or chat and it investigates, fixes the bug and opens a pull request for review. The legacy app is renamed GitHub (deprecated) and retires November 16 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-turn-notifications-into-code-with-github-copilot-in-teams/)
- 2026-10-23: Cursor — Cursor agents can now control your computer: Computer Use lets them click and type across desktop apps, not just the browser, such as driving the iOS Simulator to test the features they build. Cursor uses it on its own when a task needs it, or you can @-mention Computer Use; update Cursor to get it (https://x.com/cursor_ai/status/2113661506634305834)
- 2026-10-23: Kimi K3.1 Pro (Moonshot AI) — Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 2.8T-parameter MoE model (104B active) with a 1M-token context and image input, aimed at full-project coding and long agent runs. It is live on the Kimi API and Vercel AI Gateway (moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro, plus a faster Highspeed version), with open weights planned by November 4 (https://vercel.com/changelog/kimi-k3-1-pro-and-kimi-k3-1-pro-highspeed-are-available-now-in-ai-gateway)
- 2026-10-23: Replit — Replit launched Monitoring Agent, an on-call agent that investigates production issues from your app's logs and metrics, then attempts and validates fixes (with optional auto-fix and experimental auto-republish). Also new: Agent-made reusable skills, chat and asset sharing, Stripe Atlas incorporation at 20% off, and published apps that keep running at zero credits for eligible top-up customers (https://docs.replit.com/updates/2026/10/23/changelog)
- 2026-10-23: Chroma — Chroma, the open-source vector database, signed a deal to join Replit. Chroma Cloud is winding down: writes stop November 22, 2026 and reads stop December 22, 2026, so cloud users need to export and migrate. Open-source ChromaDB stays Apache 2.0 (https://www.trychroma.com/blog/chroma-joins-replit)
- 2026-10-23: Codex CLI — Codex CLI 0.164.0 lets you save reusable prompts and slash commands in ten numbered /presets slots, set the model and permissions inline with /model and /permissions, preview images in the terminal, and mask credentials in remote Bash commands (https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.164.0)
- 2026-10-23: TanStack AI — TanStack AI hits 1.0 with stable core APIs: an open-source, no-lock-in toolkit for adding chat, tools, MCP, media and agents to your app, with 23 provider adapters, eight UI frameworks and a new experimental agent harness (https://tanstack.com/blog/tanstack-ai-1-0)
- 2026-10-22: Vercel CLI — You can now deploy to Vercel without an account: run vercel deploy --temporary (or point it at a single file) to get a shareable tmp.now URL for a prototype. Temporary deployments expire after one hour unless you open the claim link and sign in (https://vercel.com/changelog/deploy-without-an-account-using-vercel-cli)
- 2026-10-22: Amp — You can now self-host Amp orbs: run amp orb provider on your own machines (Docker, E2B, Modal, Vercel Sandbox, Daytona or Kubernetes) so agents run inside your own network; free for individuals and teams, and free for every workspace until Oct 29 (https://ampcode.com/news/self-hosted-orbs)
- 2026-10-22: Agent Skills — Anthropic donated Agent Skills, the open SKILL.md standard used by 70+ agent platforms including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code, to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, so skills you write stay vendor-neutral (https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-agent-skills-to-the-agentic-ai-foundation)
- 2026-10-22: OpenAI Decisions API — The Decisions API is now generally available: you define a question and its allowed answers and get fast, low-cost classification, routing and next-action picks for apps and agents, up to 10x faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API, now with prompt caching, JSON and image inputs and up to 400 questions per request (https://openai.com/index/decisions-api/)
- 2026-10-22: Cloudflare Agents SDK — Agents SDK v0.30.0 runs PiHarness on Pi 1.4, so agents can hibernate while tasks sleep, park tasks that keep crashing, and recover from storage errors and cut-off model streams; the upgrade can't be rolled back past Pi 1.4 (https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-22-pi-harness-pi-1-4/)
- 2026-10-21: Recursive Flint — Recursive released Flint, a free Apache 2.0 coding model that runs on a laptop (40B mixture-of-experts, about 2.5B active), downloadable on Hugging Face so you can code offline and keep your code private (https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/21/recursive-launches-flint-a-laptop-coding-model-it-says-was-largely-built-by-ai/)
- 2026-10-21: GemDB Code — GemDB launched GemDB Code, a free VS Code extension where your code is the database schema, so a coding agent can change objects without writing migrations; Python only at launch, with a built-in MCP server for plain-English data questions (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261021228398/en/GemDB-Makes-Code-the-Schema-Eliminating-Database-Migration-Bottlenecks-to-Accelerate-AI-Driven-Development)
- 2026-10-21: Cloudflare Agents SDK — New createAI function in the agents package gives the AI SDK one provider for Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes and vendor models, with fallbacks, caching and stream resume; workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider are now deprecated (https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/)
- 2026-10-20: OpenAI API — You can now choose 12-hour prompt caching in the Responses API, so shared instructions, tools and context stay cached at the lower cached-input rate even when requests are hours apart; 12-hour cache writes cost 2.5x the input token price (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
- 2026-10-20: Vercel — WebSocket support in Vercel Functions is now generally available, for AI chat, streaming and realtime multiplayer apps, at the same limits and pricing as other Function invocations (CPU billed only while processing messages) (https://vercel.com/changelog/websocket-support-is-now-generally-available)
- 2026-10-20: Supabase — Your coding agent can now query your Supabase logs, and a new Supabase skill points it to the signals to watch: error spikes, security issues, slow queries and growing usage, on a schedule you choose (https://x.com/supabase/status/2112578077872050470)
- 2026-10-19: Claude Code — v2.1.304 adds /auto-mode-setup, a guided setup that reads your project and recent sessions to teach auto mode about your setup, warns Pro and Max users when resuming an old conversation would use a noticeable share of their 5-hour limit, and fixes claude --worktree deleting a worktree and its branch at exit without asking, which could lose commits (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- 2026-10-19: Mercury 3 (Inception) — Inception's Mercury 3, a diffusion LLM that writes 1,000+ tokens per second with a 1M-token context, is live on Inception's OpenAI-compatible API (new keys get 100M free tokens) and on OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel AI Gateway; launch price is $0.10/$0.35 per million tokens, 50% off its $0.20/$0.70 list price (https://www.inceptionlabs.ai/blog/introducing-mercury-3)
